text:
Anya Park: Heads up — after the driver rollout to CUDA 12.5 on h100-pool-3 we see a regression on longer sequences. 512/1024 tokens p95 latency up ~2.3x on production traffic, error budget trending. Putting profiling below.

Samir Patel: Oof. Do we have a direct before/after profile or kernel pick diff?

Anya Park: Pasting trimmed autotuner/log snippets — before (12.3) vs after (12.5). Note the autotuner cache key and selected kernel id changed for seq>=512.

```
# autotuner selection (before, cuda12.3)
seq_bucket=512 -> kernel=matmul_fused_sm80_v3 (est_latency=1.8ms)
seq_bucket=1024 -> kernel=matmul_fused_sm80_v3 (est_latency=2.9ms)
kv_copy_path = kv_copy_v2 (async memcpy path)

# autotuner selection (after, cuda12.5)
seq_bucket=512 -> kernel=matmul_wmma_sm80_fp16_v1 (est_latency=4.3ms)
seq_bucket=1024 -> kernel=matmul_wmma_sm80_fp16_v1 (est_latency=6.8ms)
kv_copy_path = kv_copy_v1 (sync memcpy path)
```

Anya Park: Flame graphs (very condensed): before shows matmul kernel occupying 35% of token time; after shows matmul+memcpy each ~45% and bigger stalls around kernel launch.

Kevin Liu: Looks like driver numerical changes changed the microbench ranking, autotuner picked a different kernel. But the new kernel has worse latency at our batch / seq shapes. Did autotuner include driver version in the cache key?

Samir Patel: I checked: the current autotune cache key uses model_arch, sm_arch, batch_size, seq_bucket, workspace_bytes, and alg_benchmarks digest. It does NOT include driver version or cuBLAS/cuDNN library version. That means cached picks from 12.3 are being reused after the upgrade until a re-benchmark occurs — but weird, the log shows it actively selected the new kernel (so a fresh bench ran and returned different results).

Maria Gomez: Also suspicious: KV cache path flip from async to sync means more host<->device memcpy overhead, which magnifies at higher seq. Could be a driver-level cudaMemcpyAsync semantic/perf change or a changed default stream behavior.

Jonah: I ran a microbench on a canary h100 with seq=512, batch=1. Results (latency p95): 12.3 -> 48ms, 12.5 -> 112ms. Kernel-level breakdown: matmul_wmma* + memcpy overhead.

Samir Patel: For immediate mitigation we have two options: 1) Roll back driver (fast rollback on affected pool) or 2) Force kernel mapping / override to previous-known-good kernel via runtime overrides. Which is less risky?

Kevin Liu: Rollback is blunt but fastest to reduce customer impact. Overrides are safer but we need to ensure correctness across all shapes — if we force matmul_fused_sm80_v3 on 12.5, it may be slower or incorrect for other seqs/higher batch. However, given our traffic profile is heavily 512/1024, an override limited to those seq buckets could be OK.

Anya Park: I prepared the override CLI if we go that route:

```
# quick kernel override (applies to runtime pool h100-pool-3)
rwdctl runtime set-kernel-override --pool h100-pool-3 --seq-bucket 512 --kernel matmul_fused_sm80_v3
rwdctl runtime set-kernel-override --pool h100-pool-3 --seq-bucket 1024 --kernel matmul_fused_sm80_v3

# env-based quick toggle
export REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDES='{"matmul":{"seq_512":"matmul_fused_sm80_v3","seq_1024":"matmul_fused_sm80_v3"}}'
```

Maria Gomez: If we do override, we should canary it to 10% of pool first. Also watch KV cache path — we might need to force kv_copy_v2.

DeployBot: scheduled rollback window requested: 1778102900 -> 1778104200 (ops approval pending).

Samir Patel: Proposal (short-term): 1) Apply kernel overrides scoped to seq buckets on h100-pool-3 (10% canary) -> validate latency. 2) If overrides mitigate, expand to 100% and continue with slower driver rollback or wait for upstream fix. 3) If overrides fail or cause correctness issues, fallback to driver rollback.

Kevin Liu: Proposal (long-term): autotuner should include a driver/lib ABI hash in its cache key and we should auto-rebenchmark on driver or library upgrades during node startup. Also add a guard: if autotuner-selected kernel latency > 1.5x baseline for that shape in production telemetry within N minutes, auto-fallback to previous kernel mapping. Timeline: hotfix to include driver hash -> 1 day. Rebenchmark-on-start patch -> 3 days. Canary/monitoring automation -> 1 week.

Anya Park: Action items: 
- @Samir to kick off 10% kernel-override canary (Samir) — target in next 15m.
- @Maria to add KV copy path override to same canary if needed.
- @Kevin to draft autotuner cache-key patch and open PR (start now).
- @Jonah to monitor p95, error-rate, and perf traces and report at +30m.

Samir Patel: Starting canary now, applying seq 512/1024 overrides to 10% of h100-pool-3. Will post results.

Jonah: Initial canary numbers after 5m: p95 down from 112ms -> 52ms for canary hosts, error-rate unchanged, no correctness alerts.

Maria Gomez: Triggering kv_copy_v2 on canary -> slight additional improvement ~3-5% on tail.

Anya Park: OK looks good. Samir, expand to 100% once you confirm 15m steady state. Also let's open an incident page for tracking RCA and change history.

Samir Patel: Expanding to 100% now. Rolling out kernel override + kv copy path to all h100-pool-3 nodes.

DeployBot: deploy completed for 24 nodes in h100-pool-3 at 1778102348.

Jonah: Post-rollout baseline: p95 back to ~50ms, CPU/GPU utilization similar, cost delta negligible. Marking incident as mitigated.

Kevin Liu: Next steps: PR for driver-hash in autotune cache key (priority P0), add rebench-on-start and a post-upgrade autotune job for fleet. Also follow up with driver vendor to understand memcpy/stream behavior changes.

Anya Park: Thanks all. I'll write up the short incident summary and link the autotuner logs + canary traces.

Samir Patel: Incident doc: /internal/incidents/1778102230-autotune-driver-misalignment — adding timeline and mitigations.

Kevin Liu: FYI we should also add a telemetry check in the Console: model-route-level perf regression alert when p95 increases by >40% and model infra tag=autotune. That would've flagged earlier.

Maria Gomez: Agreed. I'll open a ticket for console alerting.

Anya Park: Closing thread for now — feel free to ping here with follow-ups. :thumbsup:
